name: Shale Glossary
description: Shale Glossary is a medium-to-large rocky world whose surface reads like a geological dictionary, with every major rock formation type represented in textbook clarity. Sedimentary plains of layered shale give way to igneous mountain ranges, which in turn border metamorphic ridges that have been pressure-forged into gleaming bands of slate and marble. Vast dust seas fill the low-lying basins between these formations, their surfaces rippled by the thin but persistent wind into patterns that shift daily.

The thin atmosphere lends the landscape a stark, overexposed quality during the day, with shadows that are black and absolute against the pale rock. Sound barely carries, making the planet an exercise in visual scale—mountains that look close remain stubbornly distant after hours of travel, and canyon walls that appear vertical resolve into gentle slopes only upon close approach. The solar wind has carved the exposed rock faces into smooth, flowing shapes that geologists use as reference standards for erosion classification.

Three derelict orbital defense platforms circle the planet in degrading orbits, their weapons systems long since depleted and their power cores cold. Their design is utilitarian and bears no identifying marks, though metallurgical analysis places their construction at roughly eight hundred years ago. No record of any conflict in this system exists in accessible databases, and the planet's surface shows no evidence of bombardment or ground warfare. Whatever these platforms were built to defend—or to contain—the threat has passed without leaving a trace.

Shale Glossary's comprehensive geological diversity makes it valuable as a survey training ground, and several institutions have proposed establishing permanent field schools in the canyon systems. The derelict platforms add an element of unease to an otherwise purely academic world—their presence implies a strategic importance that the planet's unremarkable resources do not explain. Salvage rights are contested, and until the platforms' origin and purpose are determined, a precautionary exclusion zone remains in effect around each one.
